cohort: The study included 129 pregnant mothers from Dilla University General Hospital.
finding: The study found that a higher body mass index and post-term gestation were significant risk factors for postpartum low back pain.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was linked to a significantly higher incidence of postpartum low back pain compared to vaginal delivery from the second postpartum day to the fourth week, and was associated with a lower quality of life.
